name: Dimethandrolone undecanoate
lead: Dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) is an experimental, orally active synthetic androgen with progestational activity. It is an ester prodrug: enzymes in the body cleave off the undecanoate group to release the active compound, dimethandrolone (7alpha,11beta-dimethyl-19-nortestosterone), a 19-nortestosterone derivative [1][2]. It has been developed mainly as a candidate male hormonal contraceptive and, secondarily, as a possible androgen replacement therapy [3][4].

DMAU is not approved anywhere for any use. Published human work consists of early-phase trials in healthy men, which have examined safety, pharmacokinetics, and suppression of testosterone and gonadotropins [5][6]. No trial has tested it for muscle gain, body composition or other appearance outcomes in people. Its mention in bodybuilding and anabolic steroid forums is mostly as a news item about male contraception or as a hypothetical oral anabolic [7][8].

paras: DMAU has been developed as a once-daily oral male contraceptive prototype. Reviews describe it as one of several single-agent hormonal candidates, alongside 11beta-methyl-nortestosterone dodecylcarbonate and 7alpha-methyl-19-nortestosterone, with the aim of suppressing luteinizing hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone and testosterone to reduce sperm production [3][4][9]. Its androgenic activity is intended to maintain male-typical hormone effects while the progestin-like activity helps suppress gonadotropins [1][10].

No human study has examined DMAU for muscle growth, fat loss or other cosmetic outcomes. Animal work in castrated rats measured body composition, bone mineral density and androgenic and anabolic activity over longer periods [11], but this is not a test of use in healthy men. Forum users on T Nation have discussed it as a possible oral anabolic steroid, with several noting that its research focus is contraception rather than performance [12][13].

In laboratory characterisation, DMAU was orally active in castrate rat bioassays and showed both androgen-receptor and progestin-receptor activity after the ester was cleaved to dimethandrolone [1]. Work with recombinant human aromatase found that dimethandrolone and a related compound were not converted to aromatic A-ring (estrogen-like) products, meaning it is described as non-aromatizable [14]. A further study found that dimethandrolone did not require 5alpha-reduction to exert its maximal androgenic effects [15].
In men, the combination of androgenic and progestational action suppresses LH and FSH, lowering the body's own testosterone and estradiol output [5][6].

Early single-dose studies in men examined absorption, food effects and formulation differences, reporting that the oral drug was tolerated and that serum levels and hormone suppression depended on the formulation and on food intake [16][17]. An analytical paper also noted that measuring androgen esters in blood is complicated by ex vivo esterase activity and assay interference [18].

A phase 1 single-dose escalation trial in men studied pharmacokinetics, safety and food effects of oral DMAU as a prototype male hormonal contraceptive [17], and a randomized comparison tested two oral formulations in single doses [16]. A registered phase 1 trial enrolled 100 healthy men [19].

In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 100 healthy men aged 18 to 50 received oral DMAU or placebo for 28 days. The investigators assessed safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, and the study is described as a prototype male pill [5]. A companion analysis of 81 men receiving 0, 100, 200 or 400 mg for 28 days found marked suppression of serum testosterone and estradiol compared with placebo, and a difference between groups in the bone formation marker P1NP, with increases in some dose groups. The authors were interested in whether estradiol suppression would affect bone turnover [6]. A survey of 57 trial participants examined their satisfaction with and acceptability of the daily regimen [20]. A randomized comparison of DMAU and 11beta-MNTDC also examined metabolic effects in healthy men [21].

An injectable DMAU phase 1 trial (n=106) and a phase 2 trial of spermatogenesis suppression with DMAU alone or with levonorgestrel versus placebo (n=92) are registered as completed [22][23]. Reviews note that, as of mid-2023, DMAU was in trials focusing on safety, pharmacodynamics and suppression of spermatogenesis and hormones [9]. These studies were not designed to measure physique, and no outcome relevant to appearance has been reported. Longer-term effects have not been established in published trials.

Safety data come from short trials in healthy volunteers. The 28-day trials looked at effects on hormones, bone turnover markers and metabolic parameters [5][6][21]. Because DMAU suppresses estradiol as well as testosterone, researchers have specifically examined bone markers, since estradiol deficiency can increase bone resorption in men [6]. Rabbit research examined effects of synthetic androgens on liver function as a model [24]. Reviews of male hormonal contraception generally list adverse effects, injection or implant requirements and a 5 to 10 percent non-response rate as hurdles for hormonal methods as a class [3][25]. Long-term safety in humans has not been established.

Dimethandrolone undecanoate was described in 2006 in the journal Endocrinology as a potent, orally active androgen with progestational activity under development for therapeutic uses in men [1]. Subsequent preclinical papers examined its resistance to aromatization and 5alpha-reduction and its long-term effects in castrated male rats [11][14][15]. Reviews state that pharmaceutical development of male contraception was largely dormant after the 1990s, and that the NICHD, which has supported contraceptive development since 1969, funds most ongoing hormonal male contraceptive work including DMAU [4][26]. Phase 1 trials began in 2012, and phase 2 in 2018 [19][23].
DMAU is an investigational drug and is not marketed or approved for prescription. Its use outside trials is not authorised.

A 2018 T Nation post described the 28-day study as making headlines, summarising the drug as lowering testosterone to pre-pubertal levels [27]. Forum discussions refer to it in debates on male birth control and in lists of oral androgens, with some users speculating about its suitability as an anabolic steroid while others point out that research has been directed at contraception [12][13][28].

lore.intro: On T Nation, DMAU appears mainly in threads about male contraception and in lists of oral or designer androgens [12][13][28].

claims.claim: DMAU could work as a future oral anabolic steroid
claims.believers: Some forum posters list it among oral androgens and ask whether a non-aromatizing 19-nor compound could be a suitable anabolic candidate, while noting that research has been shifted towards it for birth control [13][28].
claims.experts: No published trial has tested DMAU for muscle or performance. Published trials in men examined contraception-related hormone suppression, safety and bone and metabolic markers [5][6][21].

claims.claim: It is a promising male pill because it works at the hormone level
claims.believers: Posters describe androgen-plus-progestin approaches, including DMAU, as promising results that may make male birth control available [12].
claims.experts: Reviews describe DMAU as promising for suppressing LH, FSH and testosterone but note it is still in phase 1 and 2 development, and that long-term data are lacking [2][9].

claims.claim: Fertility recovers fully after hormonal contraception trials
claims.believers: A user said that plenty of men recover fully, citing the contraceptive trials, with recovery taking 6 to 18 months [29].
claims.experts: Reviews describe hormonal contraceptive research as aimed at reversible suppression; recovery data for DMAU specifically are limited in the published literature reviewed here [3][25].

card.summary: An experimental oral androgen-progestin built as a male contraceptive pill; no human data on muscle or looks.
card.note: Investigational only; suppresses natural testosterone and estradiol in men.

quick.overview:
Dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) is an experimental oral drug that acts as both an androgen and a progestin. It is being developed mainly as a male contraceptive pill.

Human trials so far are short studies in healthy men looking at safety and hormone suppression. None has tested it for muscle growth or appearance, so its place in looksmaxxing is mostly speculation in forums.
quick.mechanism: After ingestion the ester is cleaved to dimethandrolone, which activates androgen and progesterone receptors and is not converted to estrogen by aromatase in laboratory tests. In men it suppresses LH, FSH, testosterone and estradiol.
quick.risks: Not approved anywhere. Short trials report hormone suppression, effects on bone turnover markers and metabolic changes; long-term safety is not established. Hormonal male contraceptives as a class face problems with side effects and non-response.
